item.title: Sir Reginald: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
So, on the one hand I see you reaching for a more satisfying ending… I don't think either of these two option as presented would work.

  • If you want to go for the haunting/sad thing, I wouldn't suggest suicide but instead the representation of something anomalous coming to grips with his future as a contained anomaly by the foundation… Yeah this is harder, but would be more satisfying
  • If you want to go for the whole "I have the purpose I decide" (which has narrative chops) I would want to know more about this current purpose… as I understand the anomaly, he doesn't seem like he would be much help with anything. His anomaly is that he was a fictional character which was made manifest. So how could he help the foundation such that they would buy in (along with the reader).
    • an alternative would be what is anyone's purpose? Its not such an easy answer, and it could be something as simple as existing and getting free… or trying to find what happiness he can while in containment.
    • Either way, I think what you're missing is the human connection… I would suggest fostering a relationship with either a researcher or counselor assigned to his case. Then he could explore his meaning in the world through that connection, and would add emotional stakes.

Either way, I think you have the makings of the decent article and think the rest could be ironed out in the drafting. So have a GREENLIGHT

item.title: Listener of SCP-2137: Re: Listener of SCP-2137
item.content:encoded:
So mostly what you’ve written here is the premise, but then sorta hand waive away the majority of the article’s content by saying:

This character would then go on a journey trying to access SCP facilities and finding whatever clues he can as a civilian in the SCP universe.

I think before you go much further you should think about what this tale actually looks like.

+ show block
– hide block

Nitpick:

I feel like several things you’ve said are either contradictory or just sorta uninteresting… instead of your protagonist being a “techno master” (by which I assume you meant hacker?) why not make them a lonely person who spends most of their time on the internet… instead of someone who tries to get Bitcoin (which for the most part these seem like tech Bros or finance Bros) make your character more relatable to the everyday reader… someone who has a reason to search out the foundation

Finally, I think your overall concern for this protagonist should tie into that SCP they experienced… instead of them deciding they need to see an anomaly, because why would they even know there were other anomalies?

How would they even discover the foundation? Or how to get to one of the sites? Or breaching a site?

Additionally, I think the ending would be better a little less cliched… “he searched too hard for forbidden knowledge and then died (or lost his mind)” is sorta tropey… try to aim for something not used over and over, think about other ways this could end that would make sense

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

When the two SCPs are brought together, they become incredibly powerful, virtually unstoppable, until they are separated once again.

I feel like this is the least interesting reason to keep them apart… remember quite a few anomalies aren’t deadly or dangerous at all, they’re contained because they threaten the veil. I think a different reason might be more interesting, either they don’t know what will happen or the anomalies will actually negate each other and then lead to a small reality reshuffling.. one or two of these might not be a big deal, but all the anomalies? That would be chaos

  • another problem I have is the timing: many anomalies are things that have existed for hundreds or thousands of years before the Foundation found them… why didn’t their “soulmate” anomaly merely conjoin with them during all that time
  • what about the hundreds of anomalies that the foundation doesn’t really contain at all? Either they can’t or the only thing they’re doing is making sure people don’t know about it, but they don’t physically contain it…
  • how do you intend to show the anomalies wanting to come together? Each anomaly is different, so you can’t just have a one size fits all event that brings them together
  • I feel like maybe the right answer isn’t each mainlist anomaly has another pair, I feel like this is so symmetrical as to beggar belief… might want to consider a different reason for why this “other” foundation exists

item.title: Chearleader Pom Poms[Seeking Greenlight]: Re: Chearleader Pom Poms[Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via pm
Hello there!
Interesting SCP you've got here…
Would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

So, I'm going to be honest, I love this idea. I really, really like the story, the characters, the anomaly, all that good stuff, it's perfect. So I'm going to go ahead and give you a greenlight.
However, I do have some of concerns I'd like you to take care of before going through with your idea. This is the same concern that Cybersqyd pointed out. The story is predictable, primarily because we know about the affects of the anomaly. So, the way that I'm going to suggest that you overcome this is by leaving the actual description towards the end. Maybe have the person writing the article be affected by the waves? They keep writing the wrong things? Or going off topic? Perhaps there can be 4-5 different descriptions between the addendums, and at the very end of your paper is an actual description of the anomalous properties, with an ominous ending indicating that the SCP has reeked some sort of unknown havoc onto the foundation.
Please do reach out if you have any questions about the story line/article! And keep me posted on how the article turns out. You can reach me by pm if you need help. Best of luck with the article!

item.title: New author need greenlight for idea: Re: New author need greenlight for idea
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PMs
Sorry for the late reply
Here lies the crit:

+ show block
– hide block

Overall, while I do think this concept has potential, it's falling really flat in terms of the story. There's no narrative, no event, no character that your article revolves around. You need something more than just "This SCP did this thing and this thing and this thing". It needs to be much more detailed. For example, what may have happened if the SCP did come into contact with another SCP at one point? Maybe have a video transcript of the containment breach? Or maybe have an interview with someone who discovered it/provide some solid backstory for it? Maybe provide a log of contact with aliens? Something like that. Just spice up the story. You have a solid Foundation, but you need to build up on it from there. Unfortunately, until you create an acceptable story, I won't be able to Greenlight it. But if you would like me to take a second look, please do reach out!

item.title: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
Collapsed for ease of scrolling.

+ show block
– hide block

With your response and update, I’m afraid I’ve formulated further questions regarding your concept.

To start with, considering the individuals in the center of the earth wouldn’t be able to see anything, how would they (and subsequently the Foundation) know where they were? I’m rather sure geolocation is harder when you’re literally at the center of the earth; however, that’s something else that could be hand-waved away as ‘co-opted anomalous tech’.

Speaking of anomalous tech, this line confused me a bit:

A note at the end describes how the foundation isn't pursuing this avenue of research due to logistics and a lack of benefits.

If the Foundation isn’t pursuing a way to get people back from the core of the earth, then what exactly are the people on the surface doing while they’re receiving these messages?

I’m also going to ask what may sound like a bit of a weird question: why the center of the earth? It seems like any inhospitable plane of existence could be substituted in with minimal change to the plot. This tends to be a bad sign, in my experience. To give an example of this kind of problem, let’s consider the movies Toy Story and Cars. The problems faced by the protagonists in Toy Story (getting replaced, getting lost, etc.) are problems that only toys could possibly have, while the problems in Cars (getting stranded, losing the ‘big race’) are completely separate from the movie’s protagonist being a living car. As a consequence, the narrative of Toy Story feels considerably more streamlined and straightforward than Cars.

item.title: The Blind Researcher: The Blind Researcher
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP article
Genre: Slightly leaning towards horror, but not really. A bit similar to Cain/Plague doctor genre.
Elevator pitch: An odd Researcher. She seems to have lived for an unnatural amount of time, possible millennia, and seems to know know everything that has happened in the past or is happening in the present, and always states that she is conducting research. She creates objects, often anomalous, for her research. These substances disappear when she has finished her research on that substance. She states that she wants to help the universe and all the universes, but refuses to divulge anything more than that on what her research
Central Narrative: A sample of a previously believed impossible to create chemical substance by geological researchers in the Gobi desert. This sample was claimed by a young blind woman in a lab coat, who appeared to be able to see despite her lack of eyes. When she was denied the request, she created another sample instead. Due to this, she was reported to the SCP. When confronted, she went willingly, saying "Hmm, this may help with my research. I always wanted to find more about some anomalies." She seems to know about the existence of every SCP and all secret information, despite never being informed. She creates anomalous objects to conduct often bizarre research on, seemingly out of nowhere, and has a journal which she records her findings on. This journal has many anomalous properties, but all that is written on it is basic, third-grade arithmetic. Though she is generally amiable and helpful, she refuses to divulge any information on what her research is, saying that the SCP researchers will not understand, except that it is for good. Every so often, she requests to meet another SCP, which is always denied.
Hook/Attention grabber: A researcher, whom no one understands what her research is, while creating bizarre anomalies in the path of her research. Also, she knows almost everything about every SCP, which creates quite a unique threat.

item.title: Robot Refugees From Outer Space: Robot Refugees From Outer Space
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Action

Elevator Pitch: Three extraterrestrial lifeforms mechanical in nature claiming to be millions of years old and a machine they refer to as "The Forge" have been recently detained. Apparently they are the last remaining members of their species, and the Forge is their last hope of saving it. The Forge is a highly advanced piece of technology that is the robots' main method of reproduction, able to practically 3D print new members of their species under the correct circumstances. According to the three, Earth has the perfect conditions to incubate the Forge. However, the Forge supplies itself with the materials necessary to undergo such processes by absorbing and thaumaturgically converting large amounts of matter. Due to the catastrophic implications of letting a machine like this function on Earth, consuming the world's resources, the Foundation has concluded that the Forge must be destroyed ASAP before a GH-O 'Dead Greenhouse' Scenario could occur. There is only one problem, though: the Forge is nigh-indestructible by conventional means. But the Foundation is quickly looking into ways of solving this problem.

Central Narrative: The three aliens learn they must race against the clock to breach containment, secure the Forge, and escape the Foundation before the machine is destroyed, sealing their species' fate for good. However, if they successfully incubate the Forge on Earth, it could very well mean the end of organic life as we know it.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Readers will be intrigued by the extensive worldbuilding of the SCPs and their backstories, as well as interesting characters. They will want to find out what will happen to the Forge and the three aliens, and how the story will end. No matter whose side they're on, the story will grip them, pulling them in, compelling them to see this story to the end. Best of all, this whole narrative is neatly packaged into the clinical tone the wiki's readers know and love!

Additional Notes: I would like to hear your thoughts, suggestions, and critiques on the narrative aspect of my SCP article

item.title: Humanity, for Dummies: Re: Humanity, for Dummies
item.content:encoded:
in demanding the papers the SCP now has to choose between the worth of the information versus the worth of the lives in question. If the information has any worth then it may be worth sacrificing those in danger to keep the information safe, especially if it involves operating information or a dangerous SCP.

I kinda considered something like that, although I wasn't as clear as I could've been. Part of that whole point was that the individuals were too valuable to be sacrificed. I mentioned the Site Director, but I also figured that important heads of research would be included. People who, due to the nature of the Foundation, might have exclusive knowledge that couldn't be written down.

But I definitely get where you're coming from. Honestly, papers/information was the best… excuse, I guess, I could find. I wanted a proper reason for the SCP to be attacking the Foundation, a motive outside of murder-monster. I also wanted a reason for the Foundation not to simply *kill* the SCP, and hostages was what I came up with. From there, my reasoning was that the SCP would have to have a reason to not kill the hostages, and… well, demanding information was the best I had. I'd love to hear any suggestions on that front, though.

you may want to start with a sympathetic SCP in the first place.

Okay this one's absolutely on me. I neglected more details on what the SCP itself was, because the narrative was the main thing I was thinking about. Basically, my thought was that the SCP is an android, either semi-biological or with an extremely advanced AI. Humanoid was the way I described it, but in retrospect that was a bad call. I'll probably change that, so thank you for making me pay attention to my word choice.

+ show block
– hide block

it becomes a lot harder for the concept if you need to create sympathy in a hardened SCP

Funny thing is, that was kind of the whole thing I was aiming for. I feel it wouldn't be as… impactful, I guess, if the SCP was sympathetic at-the-start. It seemed like a more interesting idea that, rather than bringing the humanity out of something that already had it, the Foundation would create humanity where there wasn't any, in a sense.

I feel like if the SCP is just a scared child or someone forced into doing something, I'd kind of lapse into other SCP's side-territory. From many of the SCP's I've read, the Foundation tends to treat those kinds of SCP's relatively humanely. The Reluctant Dimension Hopper springs to mind, for me.

Thank you for responding, though! I've re-assessed a lot of my concept and found some holes and things I didn't consider. I'll do a bit of editing to make my point a bit clearer.

(Uh, in a few hours though, it's late where I am right now!)
